sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and rese  orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K  Paliwal pronounced the following  ORDER

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 30.03.2019 passed by the II Addl. MACT, Mandleshwar in Claim Case No.63/2017 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Radhabai, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,59,000/- along Motilal vs Avinash Alias Bake on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106636936/
2 with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
Income Taken - Rs.3,000+1200/-(40% Future Prospects)= Rs.4,200/- per month x 12=Rs.50,400/-(p.a) Multiplier adopted 16 Loss of dependency -Rs.6,04,000/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs. 40,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs. 15,000/-
 --------------------
 TOTAL Rs.6,59,000/-
 -------------------------
3.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased on the lower side.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal committed error in awarding meager amount under the head of loss of estate, love and affection, funeral expenses as also for future prospects, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusal of the record and evidence came on record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants, therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on the very lower side.
The compensation under the other heads also deserves to be enhanced.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Income Taken - Rs.4,000+1600/-(40% Future Prospects)= Rs.5,600/- per month x 12=Rs.67,200/-(p.a) Multiplier adopted 16 Loss of dependency -Rs.8,06,400/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.1,60,000/-(40,000 x 4)
 Loss of estate - Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 --------------------

TOTAL Rs.9,96,400/-
 -------------------------
Motilal vs Avinash Alias Bake on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106636936/
3 6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.9,96,400/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,59,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,37,400/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.3,37,400/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE RJ Motilal vs Avinash Alias Bake on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106636936/
